title: Logical Operators
objectives: Use the AND, OR, and NOT operators
Read truth tables and build compound conditions

hook.text: "If you are a student AND older than 18, you can buy a discount ticket." How does the "AND" in this sentence combine the two conditions?

concept.heading: AND, OR, NOT
concept.body: AND: both conditions must be TRUE. OR: at least one condition must be TRUE. NOT: takes the exact opposite of a condition (it turns TRUE into FALSE). These operators let you combine several conditions in a single IF.

concept.heading: Truth table
concept.body: A AND B: the result is TRUE only when A = TRUE and B = TRUE, and FALSE in every other case. A OR B: the result is TRUE if AT LEAST ONE of A and B is TRUE, and FALSE if both are FALSE.

workedExamples.prompt: The condition for a ticket discount: a student AND older than 18.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
isStudent ← TRUE
age ← 20
IF isStudent AND age ≥ 18
  WRITE "Discount ticket"
ELSE
  WRITE "Regular ticket"
END

steps.explain: Both conditions are TRUE, so the AND expression is TRUE.
"Discount ticket" is written to the screen.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: For AND, BOTH sides must be TRUE.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: For OR, it is enough for just ONE side to be TRUE.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
When age ← 15, what is the result of the expression "age ≥ 18 OR age < 0"?

feedback.correct: Correct. 15 ≥ 18 is FALSE and 15 < 0 is FALSE; with OR, if both are FALSE the result is FALSE.
feedback.incorrect: Both conditions are FALSE, so the result of the OR expression is FALSE too.

exercises.question: When is the expression "A AND B" TRUE?
options: If both A and B are TRUE
If one of A or B is TRUE

feedback.correct: Correct. The AND operator requires BOTH conditions to be TRUE.
feedback.incorrect: With the AND operator, both A and B must be TRUE for the result to be TRUE.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: If it is enough for at least one of two conditions to be TRUE, the ___ operator is used.

summary: AND: both conditions must be TRUE. OR: at least one must be TRUE. NOT: flips the result.
These operators let you combine several conditions in a single IF.
Instead of memorizing the truth table, just ask: "all of them, or any one of them?"
